recommendation_issues.problem: Removal is defensible but the gain is smaller than stated, and the evidence covers only student data. Instructor online screens (approval lists, review and problem-report lists, device-change approval; lines 427 to 433) are the cache, refresh-after-write and refetch-on-focus case TanStack Query exists for, and the library stays in the monorepo for the panel (line 546). The phone saving is one pure-JS dependency with no native code or build config, while those screens get hand-written loading and refresh code. Either choice passes the lenses; what the plan must state is the rule that matters: student data is read only from SQLite and server data is never cached in two places on the phone. Do not count this as a moving-part reduction in the compactness tally.

Net saving overstated (see CORRECTED verdict): drizzle-orm and drizzle-kit remain in the repo for the server and #5241 is fixed in beta. The removal still passes the lenses (fewer build edits, no RC migrator on 50,000 phones where a broken migration cannot be repaired by hand), but it moves migration safety onto hand-written SQL steps, which then need their own test (open an old-version database fixture, run the steps, check user_version and that pending queue rows survive), because drizzle-kit check no longer covers the phone.

Taking the larger of the phone's own backoff and Retry-After, with no spread on top, re-synchronises phones: @fastify/under-pressure sends one configured Retry-After value, so every phone refused in the same second returns in the same second. Add random spread above the Retry-After floor. Larger gap: @fastify/rate-limit keys clients by IP by default (https://github.com/fastify/fastify-rate-limit, 'Defaults to (request) => normalizeIP(request.ip, ipv6Subnet)'). If many phones share one public address (for example campus Wi-Fi behind NAT), a per-IP 429 at class exit throttles all of them together and no phone-side rule can fix that. The send endpoint's limit should be keyed on the device from the signed record, or the endpoint left to under-pressure alone.

allowBackup: false does not deliver what the recommendation claims on this app's target (targetSdk 36). Android's own page: for apps targeting Android 12 or higher, on some manufacturers' devices allowBackup=false stops cloud backup but not device-to-device transfer (https://developer.android.com/identity/data/autobackup: 'specifying android:allowBackup="false" disables cloud-based backup and restore (such as Google Drive backups) but doesn't disable device-to-device transfers for the app'). Expo's app-config text ('no backup or restore of the application will ever be performed') is contradicted by that primary source. So the database can still reach a new phone without its Keystore key. The runtime check (database and key must match at every start, otherwise the device-change flow) is the real fix and must be the primary rule; allowBackup: false is optional hardening. Excluding the database from device transfer would need dataExtractionRules XML through a config plugin, which adds a moving part.

'Aynı imza' for instructor writes implies a device key and attestation for instructor phones in Phase 1, which the plan does not have (instructors log in with an emailed code and a session, up to 3 devices, line 69). Instructor writes need the same queue, the same retry rule and the trusted-time certificate (early close and head count must carry a provable time); the session at send time authenticates them. Requiring the student signature path for instructors adds work without fixing a defect. Also, if the instructor session token is kept with expo-secure-store's default WHEN_UNLOCKED, a background send on a locked iPhone cannot read it, so instructor items should be sent in the foreground.

verdict_reason: PASS by the rule: the research has no high-severity findings, and none of its 17 findings is refuted or unverifiable (16 CONFIRMED, 1 CORRECTED: F04 overstates the open Drizzle migrator bugs and the package saving). No high-severity miss found. Before the plan is final it still needs the 5 recommendation fixes (F03 scope, F04 count and migration test, F06 spread above Retry-After and per-device rate limit, F10 device-to-device transfer, F12 no student signature path for instructors) and the 7 medium misses (notification permission, resend after a server restore, Android 7.0 trust store, whole-request failures and batch splitting, Phase 1 receipt-QR packages, queue tests without a second runner, App Attest key failures). The research's 'zero added' compactness claim does not hold for Phase 1 (camera and QR renderer). No checked_ok item is wrong; the AWS Builders' Library redirect and its 2026-06-12 republish date could not be re-checked because aws.amazon.com and docs.aws.amazon.com reset every connection, which is low stakes.
